name: OR-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans roughly D+20, one of the safest Democratic seats on the map
Bonamici holds an overwhelming fundraising edge, about $1.03M raised versus $18K for Kahl
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold at about 96%
No public polls or expert ratings; the challenger is lightly funded and little known
model.rationale: A heavily Democratic Portland-area district, a well-funded incumbent seeking re-election, and a challenger with almost no money leave little room for competition. Market pricing and district fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: The outlook could move only if unexpected outside spending or a major late development put the underfunded challenger on the map.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Suzanne Bonamici seeks re-election in a Portland-area district that leans heavily Democratic, about twenty points toward the party in recent partisan performance. She enters the general election as an established incumbent with a large financial advantage. Republican Barbara Kahl has raised roughly eighteen thousand dollars and reports about five thousand on hand, while Bonamici has raised more than one million dollars and holds over half a million in reserve.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the assessment rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances around ninety-six percent. The race is expected to end as a comfortable Democratic win in the mid-twenties, with uncertainty widened somewhat by the absence of polling. Barring an unforeseen development, the seat remains in Democratic hands.
